title: 2002 AMC 10B Problem 11
statement: The product of three consecutive positive integers is \(8\) times their sum. What is the sum of their squares?

solutions.text:
Let the integers be \(n - 1,\) \(n,\) \(n + 1.\) Their product is \(n(n^2 - 1)\) and their sum is \(3n,\) so \[n(n^2 - 1) = 8(3n) = 24n.\]

Since \(n \ne 0,\) we get \(n^2 - 1 = 24,\) so \(n^2 = 25\) and \(n = 5.\)

The three integers are \(4,\) \(5,\) and \(6,\) and \(4^2 + 5^2 + 6^2 = 16 + 25 + 36\) \(= 77.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Call the integers \(n - 1,\) \(n,\) \(n + 1\); their sum is \(3n\)
The product is \((n-1)n(n+1) = n(n^2 - 1),\) which equals \(8\cdot 3n\)
